notes: §1985:X.5.3.4 GR5: 'A program named in the CANCEL statement must not refer directly or indirectly to any program that has been called and has not yet executed an EXIT PROGRAM statement'; 1985 states no result for a violation. BindCancel folds DialectBehavior.CancelRefusesEveryActiveProgram (false at 85) into BoundCancel, and ProgramTable.CancelNode refuses a named program with a called activation (Active > MainActive) and, through the GR4 cascade, each contained program, raising EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE and leaving it uncancelled; the never-called main program is the GR8 no-action case (PB5241). Probes at --std 85: the witness (SUBB cancels the returned SUBA, which restarts at CNT=1 while SUBC keeps CNT=3) matches its .out; an identifier naming the active caller (CANCEL NM, NM = 'SUBA') ends the run with the GR5 message; CANCEL "MAINPGM" from the main program is no action; CANCEL "SUBA" "SUBA" cancels once and the re-call starts at CNT=1; CANCEL. is refused (COBOL0001). A self-CANCEL from a contained COMMON program runs as no action, which is within the violation's undefined result.

next.reason: Same prohibition: 1985 'must not refer directly or indirectly to any program that has been called and has not yet executed an EXIT PROGRAM'; 2023 'shall not be in the active state or contain a program in the active state' (§2023:14.9.5.4 GR5). 1985 states no result for a violation; 2023 raises EC-PROGRAM-CANCEL-ACTIVE when checking is enabled, 'and the referenced program is not canceled', otherwise the result is implementor-defined (§2023:14.9.5.4 GR5). A run-time rule in both editions; the violation now has a defined outcome.
